acceptProof(bytes).details: A STARK proof is tens to hundreds of KB (§8). Every byte of it is      paid for before the verifier executes a single opcode, so calldata      may bind harder than the verification itself.

fieldOps(uint256,uint256).details: This is the constraint-evaluation cost: the verifier evaluates the      AIR constraints at the out-of-domain point, which is a sum of      products over the trace columns.

keccakTight(bytes32,uint256).details: The loop above pays `abi.encodePacked`'s memory allocation every      iteration, which a real verifier would not. These two measure the      intrinsic cost, which is what an optimized implementation      approaches — and what decides whether route 1 can stay on FIPS      205's own SHA2 parameter family.

merklePath(bytes32,uint256).details: This is the FRI query cost: every query opens a path per layer.

sha256Calls(bytes32,uint256).details: FIPS 205 defines SHA2 parameter sets alongside the SHAKE ones, and      the EVM has a SHA-256 precompile (0x02) but none for SHAKE256.      Whether route 1 can stay inside FIPS 205 — rather than substituting      KECCAK256 as SPHINCS-minus does — turns on this number.

acceptProof(bytes).notice: Accept a proof-sized blob, so its calldata cost can be measured.

keccakTight(bytes32,uint256).notice: `n` keccak256 hashes of a 64-byte scratch buffer, no allocation.

merklePath(bytes32,uint256).notice: Walk `steps` levels of a keccak Merkle path.

sha256Calls(bytes32,uint256).notice: `n` SHA-256 precompile calls on a 64-byte input.

sha256Tight(bytes32,uint256).notice: `n` SHA-256 precompile calls on a 64-byte scratch buffer.
